```{r}
library(brms)
library(marginaleffects)
library(tidyverse)

# Disables a safety warning in marginaleffects;

options(marginaleffects_safe = FALSE)
```

### Total RNA

Total RNA was extracted with the TRIzol protocol and measured by NanoDrop spectrophotometry. Biopsies were sampled before, 3 weeks/6 sessions into, and after the intervention. Each sample was measured in 4 replicate wells.

With this data, we are interested in estimating:

1.  Within condition (low- and moderate-volume, and non-training control conditions) change from baseline.
2.  Differences between age-groups at baseline.
3.  Average between age-group differences in change from baseline (young vs. old in the intervention group).
4.  Average between control- vs. intervention-group changes from baseline.
5.  Average effect of condition in the intervention groups (low- vs. moderate volume).
6.  Differences between age-groups in effect of condition.

The model-building steps (m0–m3: the RNA–tissue mass relationship, participant and leg random effects, and the group × time structure) are in `total-rna-supplement.qmd`.

#### Data, quality control and the RNA–tissue mass relationship

Weighing small tissue pieces carries real measurement error, which is amplified when dividing by small mg values. Rather than pre-computing a fixed ratio, we model the relationship between measured RNA and tissue mass directly on the log–log scale (log + standardisation, consistent with the other outcomes). This lets the mg–RNA relationship be estimated from the data rather than assumed, which should:

- allow uncertainty to scale appropriately for extreme mg observations, rather than being artificially inflated or deflated by the ratio, and
- yield more precise estimates in the well-populated middle of the mg distribution.

Quality control (applied in `total-rna-data.R`):

- **Wells:** a well was dropped if it deviated by more than 25% from the median of the sample's other wells and had purity (A260/280) below 1.8, or if its purity was below 1.5. The deviating well was almost always the last of the four, mainly on one run of plates (81–100), consistent with under-loading.
- **Samples:** sample 349 (3084 R, week 3) was excluded as a failed extraction (RNA per mg more than 6-fold below any other sample).
- **Participants:** participants who completed the intervention with too few training sessions (status "incomplete": 3017, 3092) were excluded. Dropouts were kept; their available data contribute to the estimates.

```{r}

source("./r/total-rna-data.R")

excluded                                   # should be 3017, 3092
nrow(conc.dat)                             # wells after QC and exclusions
conc.dat |> distinct(participant) |> nrow()

# Participants per tx x sex cell
rna_rep.dat |> distinct(participant, tx_sex) |> count(tx_sex)
```

#### Models

Model 4 has group (`tx`: age group × allocation × volume condition) by time effects, adjusted for log tissue mass, with random effects for participant (intercept and time), leg within participant, and sample within participant (technical replicates). Model 5 extends `tx` to `tx_sex`, as in the muscle mass, strength and protein analyses, and estimates each tx × sex cell directly (no global intercept).

```{r}
#| label: model-setup

form4 <- bf(ystd ~ mgstd + tx * time + 
              (1 + time | participant) + 
              (1 | participant:leg) + 
              (1 | participant:sample))
# (1 | participant:sample) rather than (1 | sample), so the nesting
# (sample within participant) is explicit.

form5 <- bf(ystd ~ 0 + mgstd + tx_sex + tx_sex:time + 
              (1 + time | participant) + 
              (1 | participant:leg) + 
              (1 | participant:sample))

get_prior(form4, data = rna_rep.dat)
get_prior(form5, data = rna_rep.dat)

# Priors: ystd and mgstd are standardised, so normal(0, 1) on group and time
# effects is weakly informative. The mgstd slope is centred on 1 (RNA expected
# to scale with tissue mass). lkj(2) for the participant-level intercept/slope
# correlations; exponential(1) for SDs and sigma.

tx_coefs   <- c("txcon_old_con", "txint_old_mod", "txint_yng_low", "txint_yng_mod")
time_coefs <- c("timew3", "timepost")

pri4 <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(1, 1), class = "b", coef = "mgstd"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b",
            coef = c(time_coefs, tx_coefs,
                     paste0(rep(tx_coefs, each = 2), ":", time_coefs))),
  prior(lkj(2), class = "cor", group = "participant"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", group = "participant"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", group = "participant:leg"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", group = "participant:sample"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sigma")
)

tx_sex_coefs <- paste0("tx_sex", levels(rna_rep.dat$tx_sex))

pri5 <- c(
  prior(normal(1, 1), class = "b", coef = "mgstd"),
  # tx_sex main effects (pre means, since 0 + ... removes the global intercept)
  # and tx_sex:time interactions
  set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b",
            coef = c(tx_sex_coefs,
                     paste0(rep(tx_sex_coefs, each = 2), ":", time_coefs))),
  prior(lkj(2), class = "cor", group = "participant"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", group = "participant"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", group = "participant:leg"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", group = "participant:sample"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sigma")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-models

# Prior-only fits
m4.pp <- brm(form4,
             prior = pri4,
             data = rna_rep.dat,
             sample_prior = "only",
             file = "fits/01-total-rna/m4.pp",
             file_refit = "on_change")

m5.pp <- brm(form5,
             prior = pri5,
             data = rna_rep.dat,
             sample_prior = "only",
             cores = 4,
             control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 15),
             iter = 4000,
             file = "fits/01-total-rna/m5.pp",
             file_refit = "on_change")
#pp_check(m5.pp, ndraws = 100)

# Posterior fits
m4.post <- update(m4.pp,
                  sample_prior = "no",
                  cores = 4,
                  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 15),
                  iter = 4000,
                  file = "fits/01-total-rna/m4.post",
                  file_refit = "on_change")
pp_check(m4.post, ndraws = 100)

m5.post <- update(m5.pp,
                  sample_prior = "no",
                  cores = 4,
                  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15),
                  iter = 8000,
                  file = "fits/01-total-rna/m5.post",
                  file_refit = "on_change")
pp_check(m5.post, ndraws = 100)

summary(m4.post)
summary(m5.post)
```

#### Contrasts

Both models use the same contrast set, built from population-level predictions (`re_formula = NA`) per tx × time cell.

```{r}
#| label: contrast-function

# Takes one row per draw, with columns named <tx><time> (e.g. int_old_lowpre),
# and returns all contrasts in long format.
make_contrasts <- function(wide) {
  wide |> 
    mutate(
      # Within-group time deltas
      int_old_low_w3     = int_old_loww3   - int_old_lowpre,
      int_old_low_post   = int_old_lowpost - int_old_lowpre,
      int_old_low_w3post = int_old_lowpost - int_old_loww3,
      
      int_old_mod_w3     = int_old_modw3   - int_old_modpre,
      int_old_mod_post   = int_old_modpost - int_old_modpre,
      int_old_mod_w3post = int_old_modpost - int_old_modw3,
      
      int_yng_low_w3     = int_yng_loww3   - int_yng_lowpre,
      int_yng_low_post   = int_yng_lowpost - int_yng_lowpre,
      int_yng_low_w3post = int_yng_lowpost - int_yng_loww3,
      
      int_yng_mod_w3     = int_yng_modw3   - int_yng_modpre,
      int_yng_mod_post   = int_yng_modpost - int_yng_modpre,
      int_yng_mod_w3post = int_yng_modpost - int_yng_modw3,
      
      con_old_con_w3     = con_old_conw3   - con_old_conpre,
      con_old_con_post   = con_old_conpost - con_old_conpre,
      con_old_con_w3post = con_old_conpost - con_old_conw3,
      
      # Pooled intervention deltas (averaged over volume conditions)
      int_old_pooled_w3   = (int_old_low_w3   + int_old_mod_w3)   / 2,
      int_old_pooled_post = (int_old_low_post + int_old_mod_post) / 2,
      int_yng_pooled_w3   = (int_yng_low_w3   + int_yng_mod_w3)   / 2,
      int_yng_pooled_post = (int_yng_low_post + int_yng_mod_post) / 2,
      
      # Baseline: young vs old (intervention groups, averaged over legs) - aim 2
      yng_vs_old_pre = ((int_yng_lowpre + int_yng_modpre) / 2) - 
                       ((int_old_lowpre + int_old_modpre) / 2),
      
      # Volume effect (mod vs low), within age group
      old_mod_vs_low_w3     = int_old_mod_w3     - int_old_low_w3,
      old_mod_vs_low_post   = int_old_mod_post   - int_old_low_post,
      old_mod_vs_low_w3post = int_old_mod_w3post - int_old_low_w3post,
      
      yng_mod_vs_low_w3     = int_yng_mod_w3     - int_yng_low_w3,
      yng_mod_vs_low_post   = int_yng_mod_post   - int_yng_low_post,
      yng_mod_vs_low_w3post = int_yng_mod_w3post - int_yng_low_w3post,
      
      # Young vs old (averaging low/mod within age)
      yng_vs_old_w3     = ((int_yng_low_w3 + int_yng_mod_w3) / 2) - 
                          ((int_old_low_w3 + int_old_mod_w3) / 2),
      yng_vs_old_post   = ((int_yng_low_post + int_yng_mod_post) / 2) - 
                          ((int_old_low_post + int_old_mod_post) / 2),
      yng_vs_old_w3post = ((int_yng_low_w3post + int_yng_mod_w3post) / 2) - 
                          ((int_old_low_w3post + int_old_mod_w3post) / 2),
      
      # Old intervention vs control
      old_vs_con_w3     = ((int_old_low_w3 + int_old_mod_w3) / 2) - con_old_con_w3,
      old_vs_con_post   = ((int_old_low_post + int_old_mod_post) / 2) - con_old_con_post,
      old_vs_con_w3post = ((int_old_low_w3post + int_old_mod_w3post) / 2) - con_old_con_w3post,
      
      # Volume effect, young vs old
      yng_vs_old_vol_w3     = yng_mod_vs_low_w3     - old_mod_vs_low_w3,
      yng_vs_old_vol_post   = yng_mod_vs_low_post   - old_mod_vs_low_post,
      yng_vs_old_vol_w3post = yng_mod_vs_low_w3post - old_mod_vs_low_w3post
    ) |> 
    dplyr::select(drawid, 
                  int_old_low_w3:int_old_low_w3post, int_old_mod_w3:int_old_mod_w3post,
                  int_yng_low_w3:int_yng_low_w3post, int_yng_mod_w3:int_yng_mod_w3post,
                  con_old_con_w3:con_old_con_w3post,
                  int_old_pooled_w3, int_old_pooled_post,
                  int_yng_pooled_w3, int_yng_pooled_post,
                  yng_vs_old_pre,
                  old_mod_vs_low_w3:old_mod_vs_low_w3post, yng_mod_vs_low_w3:yng_mod_vs_low_w3post,
                  yng_vs_old_w3:yng_vs_old_w3post, old_vs_con_w3:old_vs_con_w3post,
                  yng_vs_old_vol_w3:yng_vs_old_vol_w3post) |> 
    pivot_longer(names_to = "contrast", values_to = "value", cols = -drawid) |> 
    mutate(
      delta = case_when(
        grepl("_pre$", contrast)    ~ "baseline",
        grepl("w3post$", contrast)  ~ "w3 to post",
        grepl("w3$", contrast)      ~ "pre to w3",
        grepl("post$", contrast)    ~ "pre to post"
      ),
      contrast_group = case_when(
        contrast == "yng_vs_old_pre"                   ~ "baseline age",
        grepl("^int_|^con_old_con", contrast)          ~ "within-group",
        grepl("_mod_vs_low", contrast)                 ~ "volume effect",
        grepl("^yng_vs_old_vol", contrast)             ~ "volume x age",
        grepl("^yng_vs_old_w3|^yng_vs_old_post", contrast) ~ "age effect",
        grepl("^old_vs_con", contrast)                 ~ "intervention vs control"
      )
    )
}

# Hypothesis labels used by the figure scripts (change contrasts only)
label_hypotheses <- function(summary_df) {
  summary_df |>
    filter(delta %in% c("pre to post", "pre to w3")) |>
    mutate(base = str_remove(contrast, "_(w3|post)$"),
           hypothesis = case_when(
             base == "yng_vs_old"     ~ "yng_vs_old_delta",
             base == "old_vs_con"     ~ "old_vs_con_delta",
             base == "con_old_con"    ~ "con_old_con_delta",
             base == "yng_mod_vs_low" ~ "yng_mod_vs_low",
             base == "old_mod_vs_low" ~ "old_mod_vs_low",
             base == "yng_vs_old_vol" ~ "yng_vs_old_vol",
             base == "int_old_pooled" ~ "int_old_pooled_delta",
             base == "int_yng_pooled" ~ "int_yng_pooled_delta",
             base == "int_old_low"    ~ "int_old_low_delta",
             base == "int_old_mod"    ~ "int_old_mod_delta",
             base == "int_yng_low"    ~ "int_yng_low_delta",
             base == "int_yng_mod"    ~ "int_yng_mod_delta")) |>
    filter(!is.na(hypothesis)) |>
    transmute(hypothesis, delta, mean = fc_est, lower95 = fc_lower, upper95 = fc_upper, pos)
}

# Reference tissue mass for expressing predictions as ng/mg; report in figure captions
ref_mg <- exp(mean_mg_rep + mean(rna_rep.dat$mgstd) * sd_mg_rep)
ref_mg
```

##### Model 4

```{r}
#| label: m4-contrasts

# Prior vs posterior predictions per tx x time cell
prior_rep <- predictions(m4.pp,
                         type = "prediction",
                         newdata = datagrid(tx = unique, time = unique),
                         re_formula = NA,
                         ndraws = 1000) |> 
  get_draws() |> 
  select(drawid, draw, tx, time) |> 
  mutate(fit = "prior")

pred.post_rep <- predictions(m4.post,
                             type = "response",   
                             newdata = datagrid(tx = unique, time = unique),
                             re_formula = NA,
                             ndraws = brms::ndraws(m4.post))

post_rep <- get_draws(pred.post_rep) |> 
  select(drawid, draw, tx, time) |> 
  mutate(fit = "posterior")

bind_rows(prior_rep, post_rep) |> 
  ggplot(aes(draw, color = fit)) +
  geom_line(stat = "density") +
  facet_wrap(tx ~ time)

# Contrasts
draws4 <- get_draws(pred.post_rep) |> 
  dplyr::select(drawid, draw, tx, time) |> 
  mutate(grp = paste0(tx, time)) |> 
  dplyr::select(drawid, grp, draw) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = grp, values_from = draw)

all_contrasts_fc_rep <- make_contrasts(draws4) |> 
  mutate(fold_change = exp(value * sd_rna_rep))
saveRDS(all_contrasts_fc_rep, "./data/data-gen/rna_mg_contrasts_fc_m4.rds")

contrast_summary_rep <- all_contrasts_fc_rep |> 
  group_by(contrast, contrast_group, delta) |> 
  summarise(ystd_est   = mean(value),
            ystd_lower = quantile(value, 0.025),
            ystd_upper = quantile(value, 0.975),
            fc_est     = mean(fold_change),
            fc_lower   = quantile(fold_change, 0.025),
            fc_upper   = quantile(fold_change, 0.975),
            pos        = mean(fold_change > 1),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(contrast_group, contrast, delta)
saveRDS(contrast_summary_rep, "./data/data-gen/rna_mg_contrast_summary_m4.rds")
print(contrast_summary_rep, n = Inf)

# For figures: predicted ng/mg at the reference tissue mass
pred_rna_m4 <- get_draws(pred.post_rep) |>
  dplyr::select(drawid, draw, tx, time) |>
  mutate(draw_bt = exp(draw * sd_rna_rep + mean_rna_rep) / ref_mg) |>
  summarise(.by = c(tx, time),
            m     = mean(draw_bt),
            lwr50 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.25),  upr50 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.75),
            lwr90 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.05),  upr90 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.95),
            lwr95 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.025), upr95 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.975))
saveRDS(pred_rna_m4, "data/data-gen/pred_rna_m4.rds")

saveRDS(label_hypotheses(contrast_summary_rep), "data/data-gen/contrast_rna_m4.rds")
```

##### Model 5

```{r}
#| label: m5-contrasts

# Population-level predictions per tx_sex x time cell
pred5 <- predictions(m5.post,
                     type = "response",
                     re_formula = NA,   # no participant/leg/sample offsets
                     newdata = datagrid(tx_sex = unique, time = unique),
                     ndraws = brms::ndraws(m5.post))

# Equal-weighted (50/50) sex collapse back to tx level, then wide
draws5 <- get_draws(pred5) |>
  dplyr::select(drawid, draw, tx_sex, time) |>
  mutate(tx = sub("_(female|male)$", "", tx_sex)) |>
  group_by(drawid, tx, time) |>
  summarise(draw = mean(draw), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(grp = paste0(tx, time)) |>
  dplyr::select(drawid, grp, draw) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = grp, values_from = draw)

all_contrasts_fc_m5 <- make_contrasts(draws5) |>
  mutate(fold_change = exp(value * sd_rna_rep))
saveRDS(all_contrasts_fc_m5, "./data/data-gen/rna_mg_contrasts_fc_m5.rds")

contrast_summary_m5 <- all_contrasts_fc_m5 |>
  group_by(contrast, contrast_group, delta) |>
  summarise(ystd_est   = mean(value),
            ystd_lower = quantile(value, 0.025),
            ystd_upper = quantile(value, 0.975),
            fc_est     = mean(fold_change),
            fc_lower   = quantile(fold_change, 0.025),
            fc_upper   = quantile(fold_change, 0.975),
            pos        = mean(fold_change > 1),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(contrast_group, contrast, delta)
saveRDS(contrast_summary_m5, "./data/data-gen/rna_mg_contrast_summary_m5.rds")

# For figures: predicted ng/mg at the reference tissue mass
pred_rna <- draws5 |>
  pivot_longer(-drawid, names_to = "grp", values_to = "draw") |>
  mutate(time = factor(str_extract(grp, "(pre|w3|post)$"), levels = c("pre", "w3", "post")),
         tx   = factor(str_remove(grp, "(pre|w3|post)$"), levels = tx_levels),
         draw_bt = exp(draw * sd_rna_rep + mean_rna_rep) / ref_mg) |>
  summarise(.by = c(tx, time),
            m     = mean(draw_bt),
            lwr50 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.25),  upr50 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.75),
            lwr90 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.05),  upr90 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.95),
            lwr95 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.025), upr95 = quantile(draw_bt, 0.975))
saveRDS(pred_rna, "data/data-gen/pred_rna.rds")

saveRDS(label_hypotheses(contrast_summary_m5), "data/data-gen/contrast_rna.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: m5-report

fmt_pct <- function(x) sub("-", "−", sprintf("%.1f%%", x))

rna_report <- all_contrasts_fc_m5 |>
  group_by(contrast, delta) |>
  summarise(est = (mean(fold_change) - 1) * 100,
            lo  = (quantile(fold_change, 0.025) - 1) * 100,
            hi  = (quantile(fold_change, 0.975) - 1) * 100,
            p_pos = mean(fold_change > 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(P   = if_else(est >= 0, p_pos, 1 - p_pos),
         dir = if_else(est >= 0, "P(>0)", "P(<0)"),
         sig = lo > 0 | hi < 0,
         txt = paste0(fmt_pct(est), " (95% CI [", fmt_pct(lo), ", ", fmt_pct(hi), "]",
                      if_else(sig, "", paste0(", ", dir, " = ", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * P))), ")"))

rna_report |> dplyr::select(contrast, delta, txt) |> print(n = Inf)
```

#### Results

At baseline, there was no evidence of a difference in total RNA between young and older adults (1.2%, 95% CI [−7.5%, 10.6%], P(>0) = 59.5%).

From baseline to post, older adults in the intervention group (averaged across volume conditions) increased total RNA by 15.5% (95% CI [6.7%, 24.9%]). The control group likely increased by a similar amount (13.9%, 95% CI [−3.7%, 33.5%], P(>0) = 94.0%), and there was no evidence of a difference between the groups (2.1%, 95% CI [−14.7%, 22.3%], P(>0) = 57.4%). Young adults increased by 13.2% (95% CI [4.1%, 22.5%]), with no evidence of a difference from older adults (−1.8%, 95% CI [−12.7%, 9.9%], P(<0) = 63.1%). There was no clear effect of training volume in older adults (15.4% vs. 15.7% for low and moderate volume; difference 0.4%, 95% CI [−11.0%, 12.8%], P(>0) = 51.9%) and weak evidence of a larger increase with moderate volume in young adults (10.8% vs. 15.8%; difference 4.7%, 95% CI [−7.9%, 18.8%], P(>0) = 75.3%). There was no evidence that the volume effect differed between age groups (4.6%, 95% CI [−12.4%, 23.9%], P(>0) = 67.5%).

Most of the increase occurred within the first three weeks. At week 3, older adults in the intervention group had increased by 11.8% (95% CI [4.6%, 19.1%]), young adults by 19.6% (95% CI [11.7%, 27.7%]), and the control group likely by a similar amount to the older intervention group (9.4%, 95% CI [−3.6%, 23.6%], P(>0) = 91.5%; difference 2.6%, 95% CI [−11.3%, 18.0%], P(>0) = 62.4%). There was weak evidence of a larger early increase in young than in older adults (7.1%, 95% CI [−2.5%, 17.5%], P(>0) = 92.0%), mainly in the moderate-volume condition (24.7% vs. 14.9% for low volume; difference 8.7%, 95% CI [−3.8%, 22.1%], P(>0) = 90.7%). There was no evidence of a volume effect at week 3 in older adults (−1.0%, 95% CI [−11.9%, 11.1%], P(<0) = 57.8%), and weak evidence that the volume effect was larger in young than in older adults (10.3%, 95% CI [−7.3%, 29.9%], P(>0) = 85.9%). From week 3 to post, total RNA changed little in older adults (low volume 2.7%, moderate 4.2%) or in the control group (4.3%, 95% CI [−11.8%, 22.4%], P(>0) = 68.0%), with no difference between them (−0.2%, 95% CI [−17.3%, 19.7%], P(<0) = 52.3%). Young adults likely declined slightly over this interval, most clearly with moderate volume (−7.0%, 95% CI [−16.6%, 3.2%], P(<0) = 91.3%), so that the change from week 3 to post was likely smaller in young than in older adults (−8.2%, 95% CI [−18.8%, 3.2%], P(<0) = 92.4%), and the two age groups ended at similar levels.

Summary. Once tissue mass was accounted for via direct modelling, technical replicate variance was separated from sample-level variability, and wells and samples were quality-controlled, total RNA increased by about 13-16% from baseline to post in all groups, including the non-training control. Most of the increase occurred within the first three weeks. Young adults, mainly with moderate volume, tended to rise earlier and more, then declined slightly, ending at similar levels to older adults. Training volume showed no credible influence on the total change. Discussion point: the control rise is as large as in the trained groups (repeated-biopsy effect? something systemic, e.g. season or testing?).
-->
